skills.name: Water and its importance to living organisms

note.text:
Water makes up about 60–70% of the human body and up to 90% of some plants and jellyfish.
Importance:
• Solvent: many substances dissolve in it, so reactions can happen in cells.
• Transport: blood plasma, xylem and phloem carry dissolved substances.
• Temperature control: sweating and transpiration cool organisms.
• Raw material for photosynthesis; product of respiration.
• Support: water keeps plant cells turgid; it also forms a habitat for aquatic organisms.
• Lubrication (tears, joints) and removal of wastes (urine).

sections.heading: Life depends on water
sections.text:
Water is the most common substance in living things: about {60}–{70}% of your body, about {90}% of a ripe pawpaw or a leaf of lettuce, even more in a jellyfish.
All the chemical reactions of life happen in water solutions inside cells.

sections.heading: Jobs that water does
sections.text:
• Solvent: salts, sugars and gases dissolve in it.
• Transport: blood plasma, lymph, xylem and phloem are mostly water.
• Reactant: photosynthesis uses water; digestion splits food using water.
• Cooling: sweating and transpiration take heat away as water evaporates.
• Support: water keeps plant cells firm and stems upright.
• Lubrication and removal of wastes: tears, mucus, joint fluid, urine.

sections.heading: Measuring water content
sections.text:
Weigh a fresh sample, dry it slowly in an oven until the mass stops changing, and weigh it again.
Water lost = fresh mass − dry mass, and percentage of water = water lost ÷ fresh mass × {100}.
A {100} g piece of pawpaw that dries to {10} g was {90}% water.

worked_example.problem: About {p}% of Ayuk's body mass is water. His mass is {m} kg. What mass of water is in his body?

cards.idea: Water is a solvent: reactions in cells happen in solution.
example: Sugar and salts dissolve in the cytoplasm.

cards.idea: Water carries substances: in blood plasma and in xylem.
Evaporation of water (sweat) cools the body.
example: You sweat on a hot afternoon in Garoua.

check.prompt: A person of mass {m} kg is about {p}% water. Find the mass of water in the body (kg).

misconceptions.explain: That is the mass of everything else. Water is {p}%.

pick.q: Why is water called a good solvent?
e: Colour does not make a solvent.
Boiling point is a different property.
Where it is found does not matter.
pick.y: Reactions in cells happen in water solutions.

pick.q: How does water help plants stay upright?
e: Weight does not support a plant.
pick.y: Turgid cells press against each other and support soft parts.

pick.q: In which process is water a raw material?
e: Water is a product of aerobic respiration.
Urea removal uses water but it is not a raw material.
Water is used in all digestion (hydrolysis), not fats only.

pick.q: Which part of the blood carries dissolved food and wastes?
Which plant tissue carries water from the roots to the leaves?
pick.y: Xylem vessels carry water and minerals upwards.

pick.q: How does sweating cool the body?
pick.r: Heat is taken from the skin to evaporate the sweat
pick.y: Evaporation uses heat energy from the skin.

questions.prompt: A {f} g piece of pawpaw is dried in an oven until its mass stops changing at {d} g. What percentage of the fresh mass was water?

misconceptions.explain: That is the dry matter. Water = fresh mass − dry mass.
Divide by the fresh mass, not the dry mass.
